symbols.name: ambient space
symbols.meaning: The finite-dimensional vector space over $F$ that contains the subspaces.
symbols.quote: Let $\Psi$ be a finite-dimensional vector space over the field $F$, and let $\Xi$ be a subspace of $\Psi$.

symbols.name: subspace
symbols.meaning: A subspace of $\Psi$ onto whose component a vector is projected.
symbols.quote: Let $\Psi$ be a finite-dimensional vector space over the field $F$, and let $\Xi$ be a subspace of $\Psi$.

symbols.name: complementary subspace
symbols.meaning: A subspace of $\Psi$ complementary to $\Xi$, whose component of a vector is removed by the projection.
symbols.quote: A subspace $\Upsilon$ is *complementary* to $\Xi$ when $\Xi \cap \Upsilon = \{0\}$ and $\Xi + \Upsilon = \Psi$.

symbols.name: component in Xi
symbols.meaning: The component of a vector $x$ in $\Xi$, the part of the unique split of $x$ that lies in $\Xi$.
symbols.quote: Then every $x \in \Psi$ splits in exactly one way as $x = x_\Xi + x_\Upsilon$ with $x_\Xi \in \Xi$ and $x_\Upsilon \in \Upsilon$: the split is unique because $\Xi \cap \Upsilon = \{0\}$.

symbols.name: projection onto Xi
symbols.meaning: The linear map onto $\Xi$ along $\Upsilon$, sending $x$ to $x_\Xi$.
symbols.quote: The projection onto $\Xi$ along $\Upsilon$ is the linear map $\Theta$ with $\Theta(x) = x_\Xi$.

symbols.name: bilinear form
symbols.meaning: The nondegenerate bilinear form on $\Psi$ that defines orthogonality.
symbols.quote: Let $\langle\cdot,\cdot\rangle$ be a bilinear form on $\Psi$, a map linear in each argument.

symbols.name: orthogonal complement
symbols.meaning: The set of vectors of $\Psi$ orthogonal to every vector of $\Xi$.
symbols.quote: Its orthogonal complement is $\Xi^\perp = \{x : \langle u,x\rangle = 0 \text{ for all } u \in \Xi\}$.

symbols.name: projection onto Xi
symbols.meaning: The projection onto $\Xi$ along $\Xi^\perp$, which exists when $\Xi$ is nondegenerate.
symbols.quote: So $\Xi^\perp$ is complementary to $\Xi$, and the projection onto $\Xi$ along $\Xi^\perp$ exists; write $\Theta_\Xi$ for it.

symbols.name: dual space
symbols.meaning: The space of linear functionals on $\Psi$.
symbols.quote: The map $x \mapsto \langle\cdot,x\rangle$ from $\Psi$ to its dual $\Psi^*$, the linear functionals on $\Psi$, is injective, so it is bijective.

symbols.name: larger subspace
symbols.meaning: The nondegenerate subspace of $\Psi$ that contains $\Xi$ in Lemma 2.

symbols.name: difference image
symbols.meaning: The subspace $\Xi' \cap \Xi^\perp$, the image of the difference $\Theta_{\Xi'} - \Theta_\Xi$.
symbols.quote: Then $\Theta_{\Xi'} - \Theta_\Xi$ is the projection onto $T = \Xi' \cap \Xi^\perp$ along $Z = \Xi + \Xi'^\perp$, and its rank is $\dim \Xi' - \dim \Xi$.

symbols.name: kernel subspace
symbols.meaning: The subspace $\Xi + \Xi'^\perp$ along which the difference is projected.
symbols.quote: Then $\Theta_{\Xi'} - \Theta_\Xi$ is the projection onto $T = \Xi' \cap \Xi^\perp$ along $Z = \Xi + \Xi'^\perp$, and its rank is $\dim \Xi' - \dim \Xi$.

symbols.name: projection onto complement
symbols.meaning: The projection onto $\Xi^\perp$ along $\Xi$, equal to $I - \Theta_\Xi$.
symbols.quote: The endpoint identity uses that $I - \Theta_\Xi$ is the projection onto $\Xi^\perp$ along $\Xi$, written $\Theta_{\Xi^\perp}$, since it fixes $\Xi^\perp$ and sends $\Xi$ to $0$.

relations.quote: A projection along a subspace is built from [Linear algebra basics](linear-algebra-basics.md) alone: it needs only vector spaces, subspaces and linear maps.
